pr_title: demux_lavf: get total duration from track durations
pr_body:
Before this change, mpv used to get the total duration from `avformat_find_stream_info` and used the per-track duration as a fallback. This change reverses this order of preference.

The timestamps returned by `avformat_find_stream_info` are truncated or rounded or floored (depending on the decoder) at the 6th decimal place. For e.g. `avformat_find_stream_info` may return us a duration like 44.138667, whereas the duration we get from the per-track struct has a higher degree of percision like 44.13866666666... and so on.

This caused various problems such as the playback_pts being a bigger value than the duration, which would cause time-remaining to be a negative value in some cases. Or cause you to reach a negative starting timestamp when looping on an audio file with `gapless-audio`.

Moreover, we already skipped calling `avformat_find_stream_info` for mp4, so we had already been utilizing this per-track fallback method for finding the duration for mp4 files. It should be noted that while this change is only required for audio-only formats, there is no harm in doing this for videos as well.
pr_comments:
This fixes #12247 since the reporter was using ao_pipewire. This would fix the issue for any pull-based audio outs.

The timestamps at the end of files can still be negative for any push-based audio outs (I tested ao=null, ao=alsa, ao=pulse), because the `ao_get_delay` function is universally broken for all push-based audio outs.

Nice find. I also observe a precision difference in several of my music files. Smells like float vs double somewhere in ffmpeg possibly (seems weird that duration is less precise than the stream time base). I guess I'll try to do some due diligence later and check other formats besides just FLAC and mp3.

issue_context.title: property time-remaining returning -0.000000 at end of audio file
issue_context.body:
### Important Information

- mpv version: 0.36.0
- Platform and Version: Artix Linux
- Source of the mpv binary: Artix Linux Repository

### Reproduction steps

Open this file https://send.ephemeral.land/download/1643644c0c2b471e/#vE9wwIGVQxXPMiktjcdV2g. Go to the end, the osc should now show as remaining time "--00:00:00", notice the double minus.

### Expected behavior

Shows "-00:00:00"

### Actual behavior

Shows "--00:00:00"

### More information

Can be found here: https://github.com/mpv-player/mpv/pull/12243

### Sample files

https://send.ephemeral.land/download/1643644c0c2b471e/#vE9wwIGVQxXPMiktjcdV2g
comments:
#12248 should've fixed this when seeking to EOF while paused. However, this issue still exists when reaching EOF while playing through the file normally.

As a bonus, the time-pos is also negative at the start when --loop is used and the file loops through with --no-audio-display
Related question, were you using ao_pipewire or ao_pulse or something else?

060adf680627586306716f645f240b5df46d4f0b should have fixed this specific issue which was caused by durations not being reported with enough precision. Note that you can get still get -0.00000 for other reasons like with push-based AOs. See #12322.

review_comments: I know the details are in the commit but IMO a short comment would be good here indicating that we intentially prefer track durations over container durations
